newsitem.title: CAMEROON: Rwanda tribunal official leaves Cameroon.
newsitem.headline: Rwanda tribunal official leaves Cameroon.

text.p: The registrar of the International Criminal Tribunal on Rwanda's 1994 massacres left Cameroon on Friday but declined to say whether he had made progress on securing the handover for trial of four genocide suspects.
Andronico Adede, who arrived on Monday and earlier accused Cameroon of dragging its feet, left saying simply that he would report to the tribunal in Tanzania.
His hoped-for meeting with the justice minister never materialised.

"Since June I have been to Cameroon every month," he told Reuters earlier in the week. "I have given the Cameroon government a complete dossier on the matter but I don't understand what is happening."
A justice ministry source said a decision on the handover of former army colonel Theoneste Bagosora and three others was diplomatic.
Bagosora was a top official at the defence ministry during the 1994 massacres by Hutu hardliners of minority Tutsis and Hutu moderates and is he one of Rwanda's most wanted men.

Cameroon's courts ruled that in international law the Tribunal outweighs national courts and approved the handover of 12 suspects for trial. "It's now up to the president to give final consent," one justice ministry official said.
Officials said earlier this was just an administrative formality but the affair has dragged on since June.
For now the tribunal only wants Bagosora and three other prime suspects -- Ferdinand Nahimana, Anatole Nsengiyumva and Andre Ntagerura. All 12 were arrest in March and April.
